summary: The Money calendar now shows pension and Social Security paydays too, a pension typed as a year's amount comes monthly, and the file you add to your phone's calendar shows each amount.
points: A pension or Social Security typed as a year's amount now shows as monthly payments (a $12,000 pension: $1,000 a month) instead of one payday a year.

Pension and Social Security now get the same 'A recent payday' box as pay, so they appear once you type one: for a retired widow in the test households, the reviewer saw her $1,200 pension and $1,900 Social Security each month.
Pay that comes twice a month no longer asks for a payday: it shows on the 15th and the last day of the month, marked as a guess.
Each event in the phone calendar file now carries its amount, such as 'Sam's pay +$1,846.15', and changing a payday you set before says 'paydays now counted from' instead of 'added'.
numbers: Independent reviewer, second round: the widow's $1,200 pension and $1,900 Social Security checked by hand, and paychecks 52, 12 and 4 times a year and a yearly Social Security amount also hold
One small wording point left: a pension paid twice a month is still called a guess about 'your employer's' days
A new test covers the yearly pension and the calendar file

summary: The Money calendar no longer shows a whole year's pay as one payday: a salary typed as a yearly figure now appears as paychecks, and pay that has ended is no longer asked about.
points: A $48,000 salary from Get started used to show as one $48,000 payday a year, and went into the phone calendar file that way. It now shows paychecks of $1,846.15 every two weeks, or as often as the Paycheck page says.
Each payday says it is 'the year's pay before tax in paychecks', how often it comes, and that the Paycheck page can change how often.
An income that has ended, such as a retired couple's old salary, is no longer asked for a payday or listed.
On Net worth, after you add something, 'Save today's totals' is an outlined button while the green line offers its next step, so only one filled button shows.
numbers: Independent reviewer, second round: paychecks checked by hand for four households in the list and in the calendar file (Sam $1,846.15, Jordan $2,230.77), no pay line over $15,000
All three problems from the reviewer's first round closed, one of them rated severity 5
Side effect: the builders' notes for the Money calendar and Net worth pages were cut to a line or two by mistake, and still are

summary: When Needs attention sends you to Withholding check or Estate documents, the first screen now has one clear filled button for the next step.
points: Withholding check offers 'Get a new W-4 form', which opens the form on the IRS site, with 'Type your pay stub figure' beside it while your withholding is only our estimate.

When the page already says to pay the tax yourself, the button is 'Work out the payments'; with nothing to change but the figure still estimated, 'Type your pay stub figure' opens that box and puts the cursor in it.
Estate documents puts 'Name a guardian' inside the warning about children with no guardian, or else 'Start here: Will for Ana' (on a new plan, 'Start here: Will for you').
Tapping it opens that paper's form where it is, in the middle of the screen, with the cursor in it.
numbers: Tests added for how the button is chosen on both pages
Independent reviewer: Withholding check opened from Needs attention shows one filled 'Get a new W-4 form' on the first screen for three households, and Estate documents' button opens the right form
Two small points left on Estate documents: on a new plan two filled buttons show after 'Start here', and 'Name a guardian' opens a form where the name goes only in Notes

summary: Fixes from a review of the new first-screen buttons: Withholding check no longer asks a freelancer for a pay stub, and Estate documents opens only one paper's form at a time.
points: A freelancer with no paycheck who owes $15,898 now sees 'Work out the payments' instead of 'Type your pay stub figure'.
A tax bill with no paycheck left this year (late December) now gets 'Work out the payments' instead of no button.
If you file separately, the note under the W-4 button says to fill in the amount for that return, from the 'Each return' list further down the page.
On Estate documents, opening one paper's form closes the one that was open.
numbers: Four points from an independent review of the change above, each fixed; a new test covers the no-paycheck cases
Reviewer's later round, with this fix in: Withholding check and Estate documents both have one action on the first screen

summary: A mortgage, car loan or rental loan now stops counting in the retirement figures once it is paid off, and the property tax and home insurance inside a mortgage payment are counted once, not twice.
points: Will the money last?, Get started's retirement figure, Financial independence and Annuities count a loan only until the payoff date Debts shows, and keep paying the property tax and home insurance after it.

Debts and Get started ask once per mortgage, 'Does this payment include property tax and home insurance?' (Yes / No, I pay them myself / Not sure); Not sure counts the usual amount, marked as our guess.

Debts, the Mortgage page and the Home page then say how much of the payment is tax and insurance ('... of the payment is property tax and home insurance (our guess); the other ... pays the loan'); our guess for a $270,000 home in Ohio is about $380 a month.

With nothing typed, a couple aged 61 and 59 now see their guessed mortgage paid off at about 84 instead of 91, using a Federal Reserve survey of the years owners that age usually have left; Debts warns when a typed tax and insurance would stretch a loan past 40 years.
numbers: Three reviews (money, phone, breaker) and two fix rounds, then a skeptical check passed; the independent reviewer has not looked at this one yet
1,400 test households across 159 calculations: no figure you typed moved, apart from Debts' own start date and months left
Four small points left open, for example guessed loans of owners aged 75 to 85 can still run to age 91-97

summary: Get started now asks its question right above the Continue button and says why, keeps what you typed if the page reloads, and its summary says only what is actually missing.
points: When Continue is held back, the question appears just above it: low pay comes with buttons such as 'It is $3,200 a month', and a birth year like 85 is said at the box as you type ('Type the year as four digits, like 1985').
What you typed but did not save survives a reload of the tab, as long as your plan has not changed.
With only our guesses in, the summary reads 'You're set up. The numbers come next.', and a tile names only the missing part, such as 'Needs your pay.'

Anyone who says 'No, I'm debt-free' is no longer offered 'Paying off debt' as a goal; a retired household reads 'Making the money last' and is not told 'Most people do' owe money; a phone held sideways still shows the first box.
numbers: 18 stress-test findings addressed
Independent review of all five Get started changes: 27 of 31 checked closed, one filled button on every question, reload and Back keep answers
4 new problems found in that review, none severe; one is on this summary: 'Your emergency fund is thin.' shows when no savings were given

summary: On Get started, fixing a wrong birth year now removes its warning, and a retired household's summary asks for a pension or Social Security instead of pay.
points: After Continue stopped on 'We can't use 199', typing 2001 now takes the message away; before, it stayed at the bottom of the screen.
When spending is in but no income, the 'Left over each month' tile asks a retired household for 'your pension or Social Security', not 'your pay'.
Messages that point to the leftover box now spell it 'leftover', so the app's automatic wording checks pass again.
numbers: Found in a walk through Get started as a layperson on a phone
A test checks for both changes

summary: Get started fixes from a breaker test: saving from the summary no longer marks the questions finished early, saying you are debt-free removes the debt goal, and a couple is asked each question in turn. (It also broke Continue for about a minute; the next entry fixes that.)
points: Saving from a summary tile before you finish takes you back where you came from, and no longer marks the questions finished.
Choosing 'No, I'm debt-free' removes 'Paying off debt' from the goals you picked before.
A couple is asked each thing in turn, one Continue each: first 'Bo: tap the one that fits...', then Ann's low pay.
A held Continue scrolls so the question and the button are both on screen, without opening the keyboard; a damaged saved draft no longer leaves a blank screen.
numbers: Five problems from a breaker test fixed; its retest, after the next change, confirmed all five
Broke Continue on every question until the next change, about a minute later
Independent reviewer later: a slow second tap on Continue can pass the low-pay question unread, and a wrong birth year a screen up gets no way back to its box

summary: Get started's Continue button works again; the change just before had stopped it on every question.
points: The change just before reused a name the page already used for something else, so every tap on Continue hit an error.
With the name changed, Continue moves on again.
A walk in the browser that skips every question reaches the summary with no errors.
numbers: A test was updated to match
Independent reviewer's later round: every Get started question has one filled button, and reload and Back keep answers

summary: On Get started, when the page scrolls to show a question above Continue, it now leaves a little room under the button instead of putting it right on the bottom edge of the screen.
points: After a held Continue, the button stops a little above the bottom edge of the screen, easier to reach with a thumb.
A breaker's retest confirmed the five Get started fixes from the change before last.
The builder's closing note on the workboard tells the other sessions to update past the change that broke Continue, and lists what waits on claude-c's money work and what is for claude-b.
The builder released its claim on these pages.
numbers: Retest: five of five earlier problems confirmed fixed

summary: Retirement pages that cannot answer yet now show a button for each missing answer. Two typing slips with extra zeros are caught at the box. Year by year's note lists the accounts in the order you chose.
points: An empty retirement page shows one filled button for the first missing answer ("Add people ›") and outlined buttons for the rest ("Add what you own ›", "Type what you'll spend ›"). "Type what you'll spend" opens Will the money last? with the cursor in the spending box.

Will the money last? refuses a retirement spending figure over $100,000 a month. Retirement contributions refuses more than $500,000 a year into one account, counting the employer's share and the account's other rows, and asks you to check for an extra digit.

How much to take out: after a one-tap change, the green line offers "Put it back: Same spending every year" and stays until your next change. On Required withdrawals, "I've taken it" is outlined when the page is a step of your plan, and the undo reads "Undo: not taken yet". It ignores taps for the first moment after it appears, so a double tap cannot undo the withdrawal.

Year by year's note follows the order chosen on Withdrawal order, in plain words: "Money comes out of cash first, then taxable savings, then pre-tax accounts (taxed as it comes out), then Roth (tax-free)." Rows on Retirement contributions now show "Edit ›".
numbers: The reviewer tested this commit's 7 stress-test findings on a phone and found all 7 fixed
5 smaller follow-up items were not checked because the reviewer's notes had no steps for them
Limits set: $100,000 a month of retirement spending, $500,000 a year into one account

summary: Compare what-ifs and Chance the money lasts no longer give your plan two different chances. Both pages now show the same figure, and every version is tested on the same pretend futures.
points: Your plan and each copy are now tried on the same 400 pretend futures, so a difference between versions is real and not luck of the draw. A copy that changes nothing scores exactly the same as your plan.

If you opened Chance the money lasts earlier in this visit, Compare what-ifs shows that page's exact chance for your plan (80% on both pages for the sample family). Each copy goes up or down from that figure.

If you have not opened it, every chance reads "about" and is rounded to the nearest 5 ("about 80%"), and a "Chance the money lasts ›" button leads to the exact figure. A chance that is neither 0% nor 100% is never rounded to "about 0%" or "about 100%".
A note under the table says where the chance comes from. An answer that comes back after you have changed the plan is never shown as the chance for the changed plan.
numbers: Reviewer check: the sample family shows 80% on both pages, and Ruth shows 100% on both
4 new tests on Compare for the shared futures and the rounding
Small side effect seen by the reviewer: "Retire 3 years earlier" reads "about 35%" before a visit to Chance the money lasts and "40%" after it

summary: Fixes from a second phone retest of the home and check-in pages. A monthly check-in done late can now be finished, kept guesses stay in order, and the health score waits until you have answered the questions.
points: Monthly check-in: a month checked in after it ended can still finish its net worth step ("$287,100 saved on 11/11/2026, after the month ended: up $30,100"). A finished check-in now has Undo and "Open this month again".
Our guesses for you: guesses you keep stay in their original order, "All looked over" shows after the last one, and a figure far from our guess is asked about once ("If it's right, tap Save again").

Plan health score shows "No score yet" part way through the questions, with "Continue your plan: question 5 of 7". After the questions, its button opens the page with what is missing, such as "Add what you own ›".
Needs attention says "Add it on Expenses" when there is nothing there yet, and "Type your real bills on Expenses" when the bills are our guesses.
Get started's tiles now use the guides' own names ("Pay off what I owe", "Plan my retirement", "Sort out my taxes").
numbers: Reviewer: the late check-in, Our guesses, health score and Needs attention fixes work. 5 of 6 Get started tile names now match ("Spend less, save more" still differs), and the Better guesses card was not tested.
The reviewer found that Undo or "Open this month again" deletes that month's note without a word (rated serious, seen in 4 of 4 runs)

summary: Follow-ups from a third tester on People, the Money calendar and the goal and spending pages. What you type on People is kept, a payday can be changed, and a few forms now save what you meant.
points: People keeps what you were typing in the open form (for example 59) when a choice under Taxes, such as the state, saves on the same page.
Money calendar has a folded "Change a payday". A payday in the future or more than a year back is refused at the box.
The Goals form's "More details" fold fits the smallest phones. On Bills and regular payments, income rows no longer show "Edit ›" for a row that cannot be opened.
Expenses still offers its way back to the page you came from after Cancel, and says "That expense is no longer on the list" when you open one that was removed.

Needs, wants and savings saves a 33.3 / 33.3 / 33.3 split as typed ("Saved: needs 33.3, wants 33.3, savings 33.3."). On Which goal first?, "Put back my amounts" brings a blank amount back blank, not $0.
numbers: The reviewer found every fix in this commit working, on a normal-size and a small phone
The reviewer found that a payday saved more than a year ago blocks changing any other payday, with no message (rated serious)

summary: When you follow your plan step by step, the "Your plan" card on each step's page now names the step, says what it is waiting for, and asks only for things that page shows.
points: The card starts with the step's name, using the same words as the Next button that brought you there: "Your month." on Expenses.
A step that is still waiting says so in place of an instruction the page cannot follow: "Your month. This step needs your pay first: add it, or go on and come back to it."

On Expenses the request fits what is there. With no bills it says "Type each bill or spending you know, then tap Add expense". With our guesses it says "Some bills are our guesses: open See or change each bill".
A household that is already retired is no longer told its month needs pay. The retirement step with no savings on file says the page cannot answer yet and points to "Add what you own".
numbers: The reviewer found all 4 problems it set out to fix closed, for the family, freelancer and renter test households
3 new tests for the card's wording

summary: On Saving for college, the box for a year's cost now appears only when you pick "A cost I enter".
points: Choosing "Public, in-state" or "Private nonprofit" no longer shows a cost box that does not apply. It used to read "A year's cost today (for 'a cost I enter')" whichever kind you picked.
Picking "A cost I enter" shows the box, now called "A year's cost today", with the help line "tuition, fees, housing and food for one year".
Changing the kind of college shows or hides the box straight away.
numbers: The reviewer checked it: the cost box shows only for "A cost I enter"

summary: Net worth, Emergency fund and Debts now open at the right place and show the right button when another page sends you there.
points: When the monthly check-in sends you to save today's totals, Net worth opens at "Over time".
From an empty Holdings page, "Add an investment account" opens Net worth's add form with Brokerage already chosen.

numbers: The reviewer checked that the investment-account button opens Net worth with Brokerage chosen and the cursor in the name
The reviewer checked that one costly debt gets one warning with one filled "See my payoff plan" button

summary: Restoring a saved copy now refuses a damaged one. Before, it restored the copy and the app got stuck on "Opening your plan...".
points: Settings now checks that a copy is shaped like a plan before restoring it. A copy with a damaged list of people used to restore and then leave the app stuck on "Opening your plan...". Now it says "That file is not a copy made by this app" and keeps your plan as it was.
Import sends a file to Holdings only when it has a column of stock symbols, or shares with a price. A plain "Name,Value" list is no longer taken for a brokerage file.
On Rules, a rule whose category was removed shows "(category removed)".
On Stock from work, a share price of $0 now gets "The share price must be more than $0. Type today's price, or the stock symbol."

summary: Tax pages: pay typed on Federal estimate now says it replaces the Income page's figure, and saving no longer makes the button jump.
points: Federal estimate: when the Income page also has your pay, pay typed on this page says so ("Your pay is the $... typed on this page, not the pay on your Income page."). A "Use the Income page's pay" button switches back.

The reviewer confirmed one filled "Add your income" on each tax page when no income is entered

summary: Debt fixes from two testers: two quick Up taps move a debt two places, "My own order" starts from the order you saw, and the debt pages give you a way back.
points: Pay off debts: the moved debt stays under your thumb, so two quick taps on Up move it two places. "My own order" starts from the order on screen, not A to Z. An empty extra box shows a grey 0, so typing 200 no longer reads "0200".

points: Goals: a tap anywhere on a goal opens it (the link to its costing page moved under the progress bar). A new goal asks only what, how much and by when; the rest sits under 'More details (optional)'.

Goal prioritizer asks before 'Use these amounts' changes your goals, naming each change, and 'Put back my amounts' undoes it. Emergency fund's 'Yes, count it as my emergency fund' now has an Undo. House down payment says the monthly cost in its green line and keeps 'The figures' open.

Money calendar asks for 'A recent payday' right on the page, where it used to send you to a box the Income page does not have. Its links, and those on Life events, name the page they open instead of 'Open ›'.

People refuses a 'Plan to age' at or below today's age or the retirement age, and asks first when the retirement age has already passed. Contacts asks the phone for its number pad and email keyboard (still to be seen on a real iPhone).
Renovation and Big purchase planner refuse an empty cost at the box, Rental analysis needs the rent, and Vehicles takes any mileage or loan length (11,200 miles used to be refused).

fixed in a later commit; the reviewer's second round checked each payday by hand, e.g. $48,000 / 26 = $1,846.15 every two weeks

summary: Investment pages now let you add and fix things where you see them: an account from Holdings, a purchase from each fund's card, a change to a grant or coin. Removals ask first, and the first screens use plainer words.
points: Holdings with no investment account shows one filled 'Add an investment account' button instead of a dead end.

Holdings asks 'Pick the account' when there are several, says where the fund went (for example 'VTI added to Brokerage.') and brings it into view; a fund's form opens under its own row. Tax lots has '+ Add a lot' on each fund's card.
Remove asks first on Holdings, Tax lots and Employer stock, naming what goes. Employer stock grants can be changed, and each Crypto coin has 'Change or remove ›'.
Slips are refused at the box in words: a lot bigger than the shares left, a purchase date in the future, a symbol that is not letters ('acme!!'), a target mix that does not add up to 100.
Backtest says each tap's answer ('40 / 60 became $9,436,173.'); 'Glide path' is renamed 'Stocks by age'; Performance, Tax lots, Rebalance, Employer stock, Asset location and Fees use plainer words.
numbers: 19 files changed across 12 investment pages

independent reviewer: 9 of the 11 investment fixes closed, 2 partly: Stocks by age still shows '110 minus age' and 'a target-date fund' unexplained, and a coin added with a purchase date could not be lowered
a coin changed here left the crypto balance at its old figure; fixed in the review fixes that followed

summary: Estate and insurance forms no longer save an empty amount as a $0 'added', Gifting starts a new gift from one of you, and Term vs permanent's Compare now compares.
points: Gifting, Expected inheritance, Legacy goals, Health plan compare and Term vs permanent now need the amount, with a top limit to catch slips, instead of saving an empty box as $0.
Gifting starts a new gift as from one of you, not 'Both of us'. A year that needs a gift tax return only because small gifts were entered as from both of you says so and how to avoid it.
Health plan compare refuses an out-of-pocket maximum lower than the deductible, at the box, and asks about your coverage before 'Add a plan' while there are no plans.

Term vs permanent says what is still needed ('To compare, still needed: ...') instead of 'Comparison saved.', and a Compare that works brings 'After N years' into view. Legacy goals' home tick box saves when ticked.
Estate documents: the square beside each paper is its own 44-pixel button that marks it signed in one tap. Estate tax with nothing on file opens on 'Add what you own'.
numbers: independent reviewer: all 6 findings it checked closed
Gifting's 'only because split' line checked by hand against 6 cases by the reviewer
two ticks 700 ms apart both land on Estate documents; 1 new test for the split-gift year

summary: Fixes from a second round of attacks on the bank-file, rules, business, settings and stock-from-work pages: two Saves that wrongly refused a change now go through, an investments file is sent to Holdings, and a backup file of the wrong shape is turned away.
points: Your small business: Save goes through when the only change is which line on the Income page the business belongs to. Before, it asked you to type a name first.
Rules: a rule whose category was hidden on the Categories page opens on that category, marked "(hidden)", so it can still be edited and saved.

Import: the Import button now comes before the count tiles, so it is on the first screen even on a small phone. A brokerage's list of investments gets "This is a list of investments (a positions file), not bank activity" and a "Go to Holdings" button, instead of "That does not look like a bank file".

Settings: erasing the pretend plan says "The pretend plan was erased. Your real plan is not touched." Restore turns away a file whose lists are the wrong shape, with the same plain sentence as any wrong file.
Stock from work: a share price of 0 with no stock symbol is refused like an empty Save instead of being saved.
numbers: the Import button was on the first screen in all 80 bank-file and household cases tried on a 320 px phone

the next attack round found gaps, fixed in a follow-up the same hour: a plain name-and-value list was also sent to Holdings, and a backup with a broken list of people still got through and stopped the app from opening
an independent reviewer checked this round together with that follow-up and found all four fixes working

summary: Part way through the first questions, the Dashboard's rows and the main buttons on Your plan and Next best action now take you back to the question you reached, and a few home-page sentences that contradicted each other are fixed.
points: Tapping "Add ›" on a Dashboard row part way through the questions opens the question you were on. Before, it opened a single question whose Save ended the questions early and skipped the ones not yet asked.

Your plan and Next best action now say "Continue your plan: question 4 of 7", the same count as the Dashboard, where Your plan said "step 1 of 5" and Next best action said "Pick up where you left off".
The Emergency fund row names only what is missing: "Needs what you spend each month" when your savings are in, "Needs your savings" when your spending is.

The Dashboard says "You have costly debt to pay off." instead of "Paying off costly debt comes first." beside a button that goes somewhere else, and "You've been through the questions", which stays true for someone who skipped them all.
Your plan no longer says "Every figure here is one you gave us" when some figures are our guesses. It says "Some figures are typical ones we filled in", with "See our guesses ›".
numbers: 6 problems found by an independent phone walk of the real questions, all fixed here
the independent reviewer found no button left that jumps to the end part way through the questions
the reviewer still found a second, quieter "step 1 of 5" line under Next best action's button (fixed in a later commit)

summary: On Our guesses for you, you can now take back a choice, you are told where each figure lives from now on, you see how many guesses are left, and rows no longer slide under your thumb.
points: "That's about right" and Save now come with an Undo and say where the figure lives from now on, for example "Change it any time on Expenses", with an "Open Expenses ›" button.
The top of the page counts down: "3 to look over", then "All looked over".
Save stays outlined until you type something, so three filled Saves no longer sit beside empty boxes.

A row you looked over stays as one line ("✓ Rent: kept at $1,250 a month") in its place, so the next row does not slide under your thumb. The first group says "Matters most: all looked over" instead of vanishing, and the second no longer opens by itself.
"in the U.S.." with two periods is fixed.
numbers: the independent reviewer confirmed all four findings closed: Undo works, each figure says where it lives, the count shows, and no filled button competes
the reviewer found the kept lines left tall blank gaps, over 500 px after three; a later commit holds the space for only 0.7 seconds
one new test checks that each kind of figure names the page it lives on

summary: Year by year rows now say what each figure is, and Retirement contributions speaks plainly and has a proper button.
points: Year by year: the bold figure on each row now reads "$450,880 left", with a one-line key above the list saying what "left" means. It used to sit below the whole list.
Roth conversions: each year's figure reads "$21,005 to convert", and the phone view no longer mentions an "Income before" column it does not show.
Retirement contributions says "The plan adds these every year until each person retires" instead of "Will the money last? adds these...".
The small link inside a sentence became a full-size button, "See if the money lasts ›".
numbers: the independent reviewer confirmed "$450,880 left" and "... to convert", with the key above the list
the reviewer found no small tap targets left on Retirement contributions

summary: On Withdrawal order, the best order to draw your savings in is one tap away on the first screen, and the note about flat-rate tax now says plainly what to do.
points: A filled button with the best order's name ("Use ...") now sits in the first card. Before, the buttons to choose an order were a screen or more below.

When your plan works out tax at one flat rate, a plain notice says the order changes nothing yet, with a button "Work out tax at the real rates". Before, a line spoke of "the projection" and "federal brackets" on another page, with no way to act.
Choosing an order never switches the tax setting by itself. On a flat-rate plan the green line says it "changes nothing until tax is worked out at the real rates".
After you switch to the real rates, the green line says every retirement page's figures change and how to go back.

one new test, plus an updated tax page test

summary: Compare what-ifs, Advisor's plan, Annuities and Pensions give one clear answer per card and no longer save entries that could not be used.
points: Compare what-ifs and Advisor's plan: each card shows "Chance it lasts" first, then "If markets do as well as average: lasts" or "runs out in 2071". Before, "Does the money last? Yes" sat above a 37% chance.

Annuities: on a plan without its basics, the page shows what is missing as buttons instead of a form that saved a quote and then showed it nowhere.
Annuities: "This quote costs $250,000 and your savings are about $192,700, so the plan cannot pay for it today." Both amounts are now required.
Pensions: a pension with a name and no monthly amount is refused instead of saved as $0.

one new test covers a quote that costs more than the savings
left for later here: Compare showed 78% where Chance the money lasts showed 80% (a later commit made both 80%)

summary: Stress tests name the page each button opens, and How long to plan for acts on its own advice.
points: Stress tests: the button under a death opens "Life insurance needs" and now says so; it used to say "Social Security".

summary: Social Security's Save now says what it could not read, and says so when it removed a figure.
points: A paste with nothing readable, such as "hello world", is refused: "I could not find a year and an amount in what you pasted. Put one year on each line, like 2024 69,000, and tap Save again."

A table copied one cell per line is now read, and a year and amount are found anywhere in a line. The first line it could not read, and any years that have not happened yet, are named in the green note.
Emptying the boxes says "Removed: the plan now counts no Social Security for ...", with how to put it back.
A negative monthly figure, or a slip of extra digits (over $10,000 a month), is refused in plain words.
The phone keyboard's Go key saves.
